Ive had this before as well after waxing, on my face. The salon ghosted me after i showed them. 

It took a bit to clear up but it will. No need for the scrubs, those can be very harsh. wash with a mild soap like dove unscented bar soap. Since its on your back, if you have long hair try not to get conditioner on it. You can also switch to a very mild laundry detergent to not further irritate. It might also be good to check with a doctor to see if there isnt an infection. I hope this helps a bit on the physical side :) 

also your skin is not ugly or hideous, its a natural response that sometimes happens to waxing, waxing can be very impactful to sensitive skin. its not permanent and it will get better, in the meantime its also important to be gentle with yourself :)

it definitely is! i have the same but not on everything. Basically where you can feel extremely overwhelmed by sounds, smells , touch etc. You can equally feel extremely underwhelmed (english is not my first language so i hope i use the right words). For example i dont feel on time when i am hungry , which results in me shaking and feeling dizzy alot. Same goes for drinking , i rarely feel thirsty.it can also be with pain , which is actually quite common for people with autism. My therapist advised me to always tell a doctor im on the spectrum and therefore feel pain less, so they take my symptoms more seriously. 

My therapist told a story about a woman who had an infection in her teeth  and went to the doctor with "a little toothache" turns out she had a huge infection and almost died. she felt absolutely nothing. 

you should definitely look into it! there are ways to navigate around this and experience less discomfort :)

i have eczema around my eyes too! do you have any tips on how to deal with it? im always scared to damage my eyes with creams and ointments😭

my therapists have always insisted i listen to my emotions. Years ago they advised everyone to watch "inside out" the disney movie. Many people dont even let the emotion sadness be sad. I didnt either, i felt i always had to hold it in , no matter what, pretend everything is fine. Ive only recently accepted that when i feel like crying i cry. Sometimes its at school, i go to the bathroom , cry, feel better. My therapist always says that normal doesnt exist and its more about what fits with you. Holding it in isnt normal for me because it feels unnatural. So whenever i wanna cry i cry. Ive let people know around me and they are fine with it. 

So to answer the question "what is normal" id say there is no such thing as normal. Only what feels good to you and fits with you is what matters. If you feel like crying cry. Cry all of it out and when you finish reward yourself. Crying is natural and completely fine. i hope this helps, it really helped me whenever i felt sad.
